experiments.description: Market-risk Value-at-Risk experiment using a Monte Carlo-style quantum circuit with empirical marginal distributions loaded via piecewise transformations and Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) to estimate P&L quantiles.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) with distribution loading and comparator-based quantile estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two correlated risk-factor return distributions are discretized into q qubits each; a correlated normal state is loaded, then transformed into empirical marginal distributions using piecewise linear/cubic functions. A comparator flips an objective qubit when the normalized P&L register is below a threshold.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR from the CDF of normalized P&L, where P&L_norm = G1(Z1) + b G2(Z2), and VaR is obtained by bisection search over the CDF.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator-based thresholding for CDF estimation; no optimization constraints.

problem_instance.description: Two-asset market-risk portfolio driven by Microsoft (msft) and Apple (aapl) stock returns over a 10-business-day horizon.

dataset_specification.description: Daily closing prices in USD for msft and aapl; calibration period 31 March 2017 to 31 March 2021; reference date 1 April 2021; 10-day overlapping log-returns; zero drift assumption; covariance matrix estimated from historical returns; empirical marginal CDFs fitted with piecewise cubic and piecewise linear functions.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute 10-day overlapping log-returns; standardize returns; estimate empirical CDFs; fit piecewise cubic and piecewise linear transformations; build correlated normal distribution; discretize to q qubits per risk factor.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Run IQAE on the objective qubit; use bisection search over thresholds to recover VaR quantiles; compare against classical Monte Carlo and continuous reference values.

speedup_claims.conditions: via Quantum Amplitude Estimation; convergence rate O(M^-1) versus O(M^-1/2)
speedup_claims.caveats: Original QAE requires large circuits; practical implementations use iterative variants.

experiments.description: Market-risk distribution-loading experiment comparing direct joint-PDF loading versus piecewise transformation loading for the same two-asset VaR setup.

algorithm.variant: Direct state preparation and piecewise transformation loading

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Direct loading uses amplitudes from the joint PDF; piecewise loading maps a discretized normal register to an empirical register via integer piecewise linear transformations with ancilla-assisted arithmetic.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare a quantum state whose amplitudes reproduce the calibrated marginal/joint return distribution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Ancilla qubits are uncomputed and reused; conditional multiply-add circuits implement piecewise sections.

problem_instance.description: Same msft/aapl market-risk calibration as the VaR experiment, used to test distribution loading quality.

dataset_specification.description: msft and aapl daily closing prices; 10-day overlapping log-returns; piecewise cubic CDF fit for msft shown as example; direct loading illustrated with q=4 qubits for msft marginal distribution.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct joint PDF from Gaussian copula and fitted marginals; discretize probabilities over qubit grid; derive amplitudes for state preparation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare quantum-loaded distribution against classical discretized and continuous distributions.

scalability_data.problem_size: q=4 qubits for msft marginal distribution

experiments.description: Counterparty credit risk experiment estimating Potential Future Exposure (PFE) over two time horizons using multi-period quantum distribution loading and IQAE.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) for multi-period PFE

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each of two correlated stock-return distributions is discretized with q qubits per time step; distributions are loaded for each of N=2 time steps, summed across time, and thresholded with a comparator to estimate exposure CDFs.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the CDF of exposure E_t and extract PFE quantiles at t=1 and t=2 years.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Comparator-based objective qubit for CDF estimation; no optimization constraints.

problem_instance.description: Two-call-option portfolio on msft and aapl with maturity T=2 years, zero strike K=0, initial collateral equal to initial premium sum, and no further collateral exchange.

dataset_specification.description: Same msft/aapl calibration as market-risk case; covariance matrix scaled from 10-day to annual horizon by factor 252/10; exposure measured at t=1 and t=2 years; initial exposure E0=0.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Scale covariance matrix to annual horizon; load correlated normal distributions for each time step; sum distributions across time; compute exposure distributions and CDFs.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Apply IQAE to objective qubit; compare quantum CDFs and PFE quantiles against closed-form classical results.

speedup_claims.conditions: IQAE/QAE framework for estimating CDFs and quantiles
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports simulator results and classical closed-form baselines, not a runtime speedup.

experiments.description: Counterparty credit risk distribution-loading and circuit-size experiment for the two-period setup, focusing on qubit count and circuit depth for q=2 and q=3 per risk factor.

algorithm.variant: Multi-period distribution loading with ripple-adder-based arithmetic and comparator circuits

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two risk factors per time step, discretized with q qubits each; repeated over N=2 time steps; additional qubits used for summation and comparison.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare exposure-distribution circuit for PFE estimation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Ancilla qubits for addition and comparison are uncomputed and reused.

problem_instance.description: Same CCR portfolio as exp_3, used to analyze circuit size and depth.

dataset_specification.description: Two correlated stock-return distributions over two time steps; q=2 or q=3 qubits per risk factor; circuit diagram includes risk_factor_prob1, risk_factor_prob2, sum_factor_risk_factors, CDF_return_sum, aux_addition, aux_compare.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Build multi-period circuit with state preparation, ripple-adder-based summation, and comparator.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure circuit depth and compare q=2 vs q=3 configurations.

experiments.description: Noise-sensitivity experiment on the counterparty credit risk circuit, applying a simple bit-flip noise model to all one- and two-qubit gates and the final measurement.

algorithm.variant: IQAE under a simplified gate-noise model

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same CCR circuit as exp_3/exp_4, with q=3 qubits per risk factor at t=1, evaluated under noise.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate exposure CDF quantiles under noisy circuit execution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Noisy bit-flip perturbations applied to gates and measurement.

problem_instance.description: Counterparty credit risk example at t=1 year with q=3 qubits per risk factor, used to study robustness to noise.

dataset_specification.description: Same msft/aapl CCR setup; noise analysis performed on the t=1 circuit; 90%, 95%, and 99% PFE quantiles examined.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Inject 0.1% bit-flip noise into all one- and two-qubit gates and final measurement; vary noise by powers of two around the base case.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare noisy and noise-free CDFs; compute relative quantile errors.

results.unit: % relative error in 90% PFE quantile at 0.1% noise

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment studies noise sensitivity, not speedup.
